api.flutter: ContentChange's only parameters are child and an optional replayKey, and it is hard-wired to one keyframe: Combobox... no — content_change.dart's own build() always plays 'pulls-content-change' (opacity 0->1, scale 0.96->1) at MotionDurations.normal/MotionCurves.emphasized, i.e. `var(--duration-base)` and `var(--ease-spring)` per the file's doc comment citing globals.css L2904-2906.

states.flutter: content_change.dart declares no hover/focus/pressed/loading/success/error/disabled/empty handling anywhere — ContentChange is a StatelessWidget with only child and replayKey, so 'rest' (the one-shot play) is its only steady state.
states.web: The doc page's States block states outright: 'rest is the only steady state — the animation is a transient reaction to a prop change' and 'loading / success / error / disabled / empty are N/A: ContentChange has no async operation, no control to disable and no empty representation'.

disabled.flutter: There is no enabled/disabled field, branch, or Disabled(...) wrapper anywhere in content_change.dart — ContentChange only ever plays its keyframe over whatever child it is given.
disabled.web: ContentChangeProps has no disabled prop and the component renders a bare <div>, not a control; the doc page's States block explicitly calls disabled N/A because the wrapper 'has no async operation, no control to disable'.
disabled.note: Neither implementation models a disabled path because ContentChange is a presentational replay wrapper around arbitrary content, not an interactive control — n/a on both sides for the same reason, not a missing feature.

interaction.flutter: KeyframePlayer is given key: ValueKey(replayKey) when replayKey is non-null, and Flutter's key mechanism causes the element to be treated as a new widget instance when the key value changes — i.e. the animated subtree is torn down and rebuilt, per Flutter's own reconciliation rules for a changed key.
interaction.web: The file's own 'WHY REMOVE / REFLOW / RE-ADD' doc comment is explicit: 'ContentChange deliberately does not remount: ... A remount would throw away focus and scroll position inside children' — the ref-held DOM node survives every contentKey change untouched, only its class list is toggled.

semantics.flutter: ContentChange.build() returns KeyframePlayer directly with no Semantics(...) wrapper, no semanticLabel, and no role — it is purely visual, forwarding whatever accessibility tree child itself produces.
semantics.web: The rendered <div data-slot="content-change"> carries no role, aria-* attribute, or accessible name of its own beyond {...props} passthrough — it is a transparent wrapper around children's own semantics.
semantics.note: Both sides are semantics-transparent wrappers with no accessible name, role, or announcement of their own — there is nothing to compare because neither one participates in the accessibility tree beyond passing children through.
